item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: April 09, 2026
item.description:
Here are the key items from the Austin City Council agenda, summarized in 4 bullet points: * **Utility Rate Suspensions:** Council will vote on suspending proposed interim rate increases from Atmos Energy and Texas Gas Service, which could impact gas utility customer bills. * **Parkland & Traffic Infrastructure:** Decisions include approving the acquisition of 49 acres for new parkland and accepting over $13 million in state grants for significant traffic system upgrades, including monitoring and smart signal technology. * **Land Use & City Boundaries:** Public hearings will be held on authorizing eminent domain for a new regional public safety communications tower and on disannexing multiple properties from the city limits under state law. * **Zoning Changes for Development:** Council will conduct public hearings and consider action on several zoning requests across the city, many proposing to convert single-family or commercial areas to mixed-use or higher-density residential. One contentious item involves a request for commercial-liquor sales zoning with public opposition.

item.title: Austin Austin Housing Finance Corporation: April 09, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation agenda: * The Austin Housing Finance Corporation plans to authorize **over $35 million in new funding** to boost affordable housing efforts in Austin. * **Over $29 million will be dedicated to new affordable housing developments**, including projects like Ada Anderson Place, Goodnight Ranch, South First Affordable Apartments, and Verbena Flats, creating both homeownership and rental opportunities. * The Corporation will vote on **transferring city-owned land** on Tannehill Lane to a non-profit developer to build approximately 32 new affordable ownership units. * An additional **$6 million is proposed for the Local Housing Voucher Program**, significantly expanding direct housing assistance for qualifying Austin residents and families.

item.title: Austin Work Session: April 07, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council Work Session agenda: * **Key Briefing on Police Use of Force:** The Council's primary focus will be an update from the Austin Police Use of Force Task Force, presented by an expert from The Ohio State University. This briefing is expected to cover ongoing efforts and potential recommendations regarding police conduct. * **Work Session for Discussion:** This meeting is a work session, meaning the Council will primarily discuss and receive information on various city issues and briefings, rather than making immediate votes on new policies. * **General Council Discussions:** Council members will also have time to discuss pre-selected agenda items and other topics of interest to the city.

item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda in 3-5 bullet points, focusing on key items, public hearings, and policy decisions: * **Major Housing and Development Reforms:** Council will consider initiating significant changes to zoning laws to allow more diverse housing types ("missing middle housing") and mixed-use developments, along with exploring policies to reduce or unbundle parking requirements to boost affordability and transit use. * **Strategic Planning for Homelessness and Transportation:** The agenda includes adopting a new 2025-2027 Strategic Plan to address homelessness and holding a public hearing on updating the Austin Core Transportation Plan. * **Public Hearings on Land Use and City Boundaries:** The Council will hear public input on amending city billboard regulations, consider changing the use of parkland at Auditorium Shores for a water line, and address numerous small property disannexations from city limits under a new state law. * **Support for Small Businesses:** Proposals are on the table to expand economic opportunities for small businesses by updating regulations for home-based businesses and allowing Accessory Commercial Units.

item.title: Austin Work Session: March 24, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Major Housing Policy Overhaul:** Council will consider initiating significant changes to city zoning rules to allow more diverse and smaller housing types (like townhomes and cottage courts, known as "missing middle housing") and developments that combine residential and commercial uses. * **Homelessness Strategic Plan:** Discussion of the new 2025-2027 Strategic Plan, which provides a framework for addressing homelessness in Austin. * **Public Hearing on Sign Regulations:** A public hearing will be held on proposed changes to allow larger electronic signs, including those with off-premises advertising, in public areas. * **I-35 Cap and Stitch Project Update:** Council will receive a briefing on the latest recommendations for the I-35 Cap and Stitch project.

item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 12, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda in 3-5 bullet points: * **Potential Rezoning of City Golf Courses:** Council will consider initiating a rezoning process for the Jimmy Clay and Roy Kizer Golf Courses, a significant step that could change their future land use. * **Major Land Use Hearings & Disannexations:** Public hearings are scheduled for numerous land use changes, including proposals for new mixed-use developments in various districts, and property disannexations under State Senate Bill 1844. * **Substantial Water Infrastructure Investments:** Council will consider approving significant funding for Austin Water, including increasing a low-interest federal loan to nearly $1 billion for the Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant expansion and authorizing $575 million in water and wastewater revenue bonds. * **Policy and Economic Development Items:** Agenda includes updates to lobbyist regulations, a financial agreement to support local creative business The Vortex, and amendments for a large affordable housing development at 800 E. St. John Avenue.
